arxiv-1903-08543.title: Optimizing thermodynamic trajectories using evolutionary and gradient-based reinforcement learning
arxiv-1903-08543.creator: Chris Beeler 1,2, Uladzimir Yahorau 3, Rory Coles 4, Kyle Mills 3,5, Stephen Whitelam 6, Isaac Tamblyn 1,3,5
arxiv-1903-08543.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Chris Beeler 1,2, Uladzimir Yahorau 3, Rory Coles 4, Kyle Mills 3,5, Stephen Whitelam 6, Isaac Tamblyn 1,3,5. Using a model heat engine, we show that neural network-based reinforcement learning can identify thermodynamic trajectories of maximal efficiency. We consider both gradient and gradient-free reinforcement learning.

arxiv-2010-03638.title: Stäckel Equivalence of Non-Degenerate Superintegrable Systems, and Invariant Quadrics
arxiv-2010-03638.creator: Andreas VOLLMER †‡
arxiv-2010-03638.description: Abstract A non-degenerate second-order maximally conformally superintegrable system in dimension 2 naturally gives rise to a quadric with position dependent coefficients. It is shown how the system’s Stäckel class can be obtained from this associated quadric. The Stäckel class of a second-order maximally conformally superintegrable system is its equivalence class under Stäckel transformations, i.e., under coupling-constant metamorphosis.

arxiv-2103-12343.title: Skyrmion-size dependence of the topological Hall effect: A real-space calculation
arxiv-2103-12343.creator: Akira Matsui, Takuya Nomoto, Ryotaro Arita
arxiv-2103-12343.description: Abstract Motivated by the recent discoveries of magnets harboring short-pitch skyrmion lattices, we investigate the skyrmion-size dependence of the topological Hall effect. By means of large-scale real-space calculations, we find that the Hall conductivity takes its extreme value in the crossover region where both the real-space and momentum-space Berry curvature play a crucial role.

arxiv-2109-03462.title: Recalibrating the KITTI Dataset Camera Setup for Improved Odometry Accuracy
arxiv-2109-03462.creator: Igor Cvišić, Ivan Marković and Ivan Petrović
arxiv-2109-03462.description: Abstract Over the last decade, one of the most relevant public datasets for evaluating odometry accuracy is the KITTI dataset. Beside the quality and rich sensor setup, its success is also due to the online evaluation tool, which enables researchers to benchmark and compare algorithms.

arxiv-2401-12421.title: AdaEmbed: Semi-supervised Domain Adaptation in the Embedding Space
arxiv-2401-12421.creator: Ali Mottaghi mottaghi@stanford.eduStanford University, Stanford, CA Mohammad Abdullah Jamal abdullah.jamal@intusurg.comIntuitive Surgical Inc., Sunnyvale, CA, Serena Yeung syyeung@stanford.eduStanford University, Stanford, CA, Omid Mohareri omid.mohareri@intusurg.comIntuitive Surgical Inc., Sunnyval
arxiv-2401-12421.description: Abstract Semi-supervised domain adaptation (SSDA) presents a critical hurdle in computer vision, especially given the frequent scarcity of labeled data in real-world settings. This scarcity often causes foundation models, trained on extensive datasets, to underperform when applied to new domains. AdaEmbed, our newly proposed methodology for SSDA, offers a promising solution to these challenges.

arxiv-2406-06870.title: What’s in an embedding? Would a rose by any embedding smell as sweet?
arxiv-2406-06870.creator: Venkat Venkatasubramanian
arxiv-2406-06870.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Venkat Venkatasubramanian. Abstract

Large Language Models (LLMs) are often criticized for lacking true ”understanding” and the ability to ”reason” with their knowledge, being seen merely as autocomplete systems. We believe that this assessment might be missing a nuanced insight. We suggest that LLMs do develop a kind of empirical ”understanding” that is ”geometry”-like, which seems adequate for a range of applications in NLP, computer vision, coding assistance, etc.

arxiv-2502-00288.title: Learning from Suboptimal Data in Continuous Control via Auto-Regressive Soft Q-Network
arxiv-2502-00288.creator: Jijia Liu, Feng Gao, Qingmin Liao, Chao Yu, Yu Wang
arxiv-2502-00288.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) for continuous control often requires large amounts of online interaction data. Value-based RL methods can mitigate this burden by offering relatively high sample efficiency. Some studies further enhance sample efficiency by incorporating offline demonstration data to “kick-start” training, achieving promising results in continuous control.

arxiv-2511-22158.title: Quantum Simulation of Ligand-like Molecules through Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization in Density Matrix Embedding Framework
arxiv-2511-22158.creator: Ashish Kumar Patra, Anurag K. S. V., Sai Shankar P., Ruchika Bhat, Raghavendra V., Rahul Maitra, Jaiganesh G.
arxiv-2511-22158.description: Abstract The accurate treatment of electron correlation in extended molecular systems remains computationally challenging using classical electronic structure methods. Hybrid quantum–classical algorithms offer a potential route to overcome these limitations; however, their practical deployment on existing quantum computers requires strategies that both reduce problem size and mitigate hardware noise.

pmc-11607326.creator: Wei Fang, Kun Ren, Tiejun Liu, Jianan Shang, Shengce Jia, Xiangxiang Jiang, Jie Zhang

pmc-12627662.title: Federated task-adaptive learning for personalized selection of human IVF-derived embryos
pmc-12627662.creator: Tianrun Gao, Yuning Yang, Kai Wang, Yuanxu Gao, Lishuang Ma, Lei Chen, Guangdong Liu, Ping Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Guangyu Wang
pmc-12627662.description: BackgroundIn-vitro fertilization (IVF) provides an effective infertility treatment. However, the success of IVF heavily depends on manual morphological assessment of embryos, a process that is both time-consuming and labor-intensive. While artificial intelligence (AI) enables automated assessment, its reliance on centralized large-scale data training raises privacy concerns.

pmc-12639405.creator: Sungwoo Kang, Seun Jeon, Yeoju Kim, Su‐Hee Jeon, Minsun Choi, Young‐gun Lee, Byoung Seok Ye, for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
pmc-12639405.description: INTRODUCTIONThe clinical implications of brain hypermetabolism remain unexplored in Lewy body disease (LBD) co‐pathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD).METHODSWe investigated cognition, 18F‐fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (PET), and cerebrospinal fluid tau phosphorylated at threonine 181 (pTau181)/Aβ42 plus α‐synuclein seeding amplification assays (SAA) in controls, 217 SAA‐negative AD (ADSAA−), and 124 SAA‐positive AD (ADSAA+).

pmc-12973037.title: Navigation-Assisted Percutaneous Fixation of an Anterior Column and Posterior Hemitransverse Fracture in an Elderly Patient: A Case Report
pmc-12973037.creator: Matthew Rohl, Taylor J Manes, Nate Rodriguez, Kevin Monahan, Joseph P Scheschuk
pmc-12973037.description: Introduction:Acetabular fractures in elderly patients are often the result of low-energy trauma and are complicated by osteopenia, comorbidities, and limited physiologic reserve. Minimally invasive approaches, such as percutaneous fixation have emerged as viable alternatives to open reduction in selected fracture patterns.

pmc-12980901.creator: Derya Özbaş Gençarslan, Eda Açıkgöz Atay, Songül Nida Kaplan, Ayşe Duygu Özbaş, Melike Yavaş Çelik, Özlem Işıl
pmc-12980901.description: BackgroundAlthough pregnancy is a part of the natural life cycle for every woman, the idea that pregnancy is a happy period and a state of emotional well-being has now been abandoned. This process causes intense changes to woman bodies, minds and society.

pmc-13222769.title: Treatment Satisfaction with Tenapanor: Real-World Survey of Patients with End-Stage Renal Disease and Hyperphosphatemia
pmc-13222769.creator: Jessica B Kendrick, Luisa L Scott, Belinda Gist, Laura A Williams
pmc-13222769.description: PurposeTenapanor (XPHOZAH), approved by the US FDA in October 2023, is indicated to reduce serum phosphorus in adults with chronic kidney disease on dialysis as add-on therapy in patients who have an inadequate response to or are intolerant of any dose of phosphate binders. Unlike phosphate binders, tenapanor inhibits phosphate absorption by reducing permeability through the paracellular pathway.

pmc-13258719.title: From Molecules to Biomarkers: Nogo Proteins and Receptors in the Early Detection of Type 2 Diabetes Complications: A Systematic Review
pmc-13258719.creator: Jelena M. Bogdanović, Ivana Babić, Jelena Stanarčić Gajović, Sandra Singh Lukač, Dragana Mijač, Dušan Popović, Ivan Ranković, Ljiljana Popović, Iva Rasulić, Katarina Lalić
pmc-13258719.description: Nogo (RTN4) proteins and their receptors have emerged as candidate mediators of metabolic regulation and vascular pathology relevant to type 2 diabetes (T2D). The primary objective of this PRISMA-guided systematic review was to evaluate the clinical and cohort evidence for RTN4/RTN4R as potential biomarkers of T2D progression and vascular complications.

pmc-13353894.creator: Matheus A. Tunes, Martin Hasenburger, Rostislav Daniel, Oscar M. Prada‐Ramirez, Philip Aster, Sebastian Samberger, Thomas M. Kremmer, Johannes A. Österreicher
pmc-13353894.description: Differential phase contrast (DPC) imaging in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) maps projected electric/magnetic fields through the phase sensitivity of segmented low‐angle detectors. Although typically applied to atomic‐resolution imaging at low beam currents, STEM‐DPC is here demonstrated as a rapid micro and nanoscale image‐segmentation tool for materials characterization with particular focus on advanced aluminum alloys.

pmc-13357137.title: Unmasking biomarkers in small cell lung cancer: implication for precision oncology
pmc-13357137.creator: Devshree Parganiha, Mohit Joshi, Sivaramasundaram Sankarasubramanian, Sharanya V Pandit, Harishmitha Nagaraj, Naveenkumar Perumal
pmc-13357137.description: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) ranks among the most aggressive cancers, posing significant challenges in early diagnosis and treatment with limited therapeutic options. Smoking is one of the major risk factors, which constitutes a substantial proportion of lung cancer cases globally.

pmc-13453349.title: The Interplay Between Self-Determination and Cognitive Bias: Nonlinear Associations Between Myopia Control Knowledge Reserve and Parental Communication Preparedness
pmc-13453349.creator: Yang Chen, Yijia He, Shenyu Zhao, Jing Zhou, Siyuan Wu, Xiyang Xia, Lingmin Hu, Renjie Lu
pmc-13453349.description: ObjectiveParents bear statutory proxy responsibilities during adolescent myopia diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to reveal the relationship between myopia control knowledge reserve (KR) and parental communication preparedness (CP), explore the moderating role of the Dunning-Kruger effect within the self-determination theory (SDT) framework, thereby providing theoretical foundations for optimizing myopia control strategies.
